actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 15 (2d10 + 4) piercing damage.

actions.name: Hooves
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 13 (2d8 + 4) bludgeoning damage.

actions.name: Cry of the Margreve
actions.description: The colláis sounds a dreadful and reverberating call. Each creature within 100 feet of the colláis that can hear the cry must succeed on a DC 16 Charisma saving throw or be frightened until the end of its next turn. If a creature's saving throw is successful or the effect ends for it, the creature is immune to the colláis's Cry of the Margreve for the next 24 hours. Forest-dwelling beasts and monstrosities with an Intelligence of 4 or lower automatically succeed or fail on this saving throw, depending on the colláis's choice.

monsters.name: Vine Golem
damage_resistances: bludgeoning and piercing from nonmagical attacks not made with adamantine weapons
languages: understands the languages of its creator but can't speak

features.name: Bound
features.description: The vine golem is psychically bound to its creator and can communicate telepathically with its creator as long as neither is incapacitated. In addition, each knows the distance and direction to the other. The golem and its creator don't have to be on the same plane of existence to communicate telepathically, but they do have to be on the same plane to know the distance and direction to each other.

features.description: When the piney hits with any weapon while within the boundaries of the Margreve, the weapon deals an extra 3 (1d6) force damage (included in the attack).

features.name: Verdant Transformation
features.description:

Oaken Flesh. The piney’s Armor Class increases by 2, and it has resistance to bludgeoning damage until the start of its next turn.

actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) bludgeoning damage plus 3 (1d6) force damage.

features.name: Force of Nature
features.description: When the piney rootwalker hits with any weapon while within the boundaries of the Margreve, the weapon deals an extra 7 (2d6) force damage (included in the attack).

features.name: One with the Woods
features.description: While in a forest, the piney rootwalker can't be tracked. In addition, the piney rootwalker has advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks made to hide in forest terrain.

features.name: Innate Spellcasting
features.description:
The piney rootwalker's innate spellcasting ability is Wisdom (spell save DC 13). It can innately cast the following spells, requiring no material components.
At will: mending, poison spray, resistance
2/day each: entangle, healing word
1/day each: locate animals or plants, spike growth

actions.name: Slam
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) bludgeoning damage plus 7 (2d6) force damage.

actions.name: Rock
actions.description: Ranged Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, range 60/240 ft., one target. Hit: 9 (1d10 + 4) bludgeoning damage plus 7 (2d6) force damage.

features.name: Iron Scent
features.description: The boar can pinpoint, by scent, the location of ferrous metal within 60 feet of it.

features.name: Lightning Hide
features.description: A creature that touches the boar or hits it with a melee attack while within 5 feet of it takes 5 (2d4) lightning damage.

features.name: Relentless (Recharges after a Short or Long Rest)
features.description: If the boar takes 15 damage or less that would reduce it to 0 hp, it is reduced to 1 hp instead.

features.name: Thunder Charge
features.description: If the boar moves at least 20 feet straight toward a target and then hits it with a tusk attack on the same turn, the target takes an extra 11 (2d10) thunder damage. If the target is a creature, it must succeed on a DC 15 Strength saving throw or be knocked prone.

actions.name: Tusk
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) slashing damage and 11 (2d10) lightning damage. In addition, nonmagical metal armor worn by the target is partly devoured by the boar and takes a permanent and cumulative −2 penalty to the AC it offers. The armor is destroyed if the penalty reduces its AC to 10.

actions.name: Lightning Run (Recharge 6)
actions.description: The boar becomes a bolt of living lightning and moves up to its speed without provoking opportunity attacks. It can move through creatures and objects as if they were difficult terrain. It takes 5 (1d10) force damage and is pushed to the closest unoccupied space if it ends its turn inside an object. Each creature in the boar's path must make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw, taking 22 (4d10) lightning damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

actions.name: Thunder Leap (Recharge 6)
actions.description: The boar moves up to 20 feet, jumping over obstacles in its way. Difficult terrain doesn't cost it extra movement when it leaps. Each creature within 10 feet of the boar when it leaps and each creature within 10 feet of where it lands must make a DC 15 Constitution saving throw. On a failure, a creature takes 16 (3d10) thunder damage and is pushed up to 10 feet away from the boar. On a success, a creature takes half the damage and isn't pushed.

monsters.name: Tree Skinner
damage_resistances: bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks not made with silvered weapons

features.name: False Appearance (Tree Form Only)
features.description: While the skinner remains motionless, it is indistinguishable from a normal tree.

features.name: Inhabit Tree
features.description: As a bonus action, the skinner touches a Medium or larger tree that is not a creature and disappears inside it. While inside the tree, the skinner has tremorsense with a radius of 30 feet, has an AC of 15, has a speed of 0, and has vulnerability to fire damage. When the skinner is reduced to 15 hp, the tree dies and the skinner appears within 5 feet of the dead tree or in the nearest unoccupied space. The skinner can exit the tree as a bonus action, appearing within 5 feet of the tree in the nearest unoccupied space, and the tree reverts to being an object. The skinner can inhabit a tree for only 3 days at most before the tree dies, requiring the skinner to seek another vessel.

features.name: Magic Resistance
features.description: The skinner has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

actions.name: Claw
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) slashing damage. The target must succeed on a DC 13 Constitution saving throw or take 7 (2d6) poison damage and become poisoned until the end of its next turn.

actions.name: Vine Whip (Tree Form Only)
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. Hit: 10 (2d6 + 3) bludgeoning damage, and if the target is a Large or smaller creature, it is grappled (escape DC 13). The skinner can grapple up to two creatures at one time.

actions.name: Squeeze (Tree Form Only)
actions.description: The tree skinner makes one vine whip attack against a creature it is grappling. If the attack hits, the target is also unable to breathe or cast spells with verbal components until this grapple ends.

features.name: Keen Smell
features.description: The tsuchinoko has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on smell.

features.name: Plant Camouflage
features.description: The tsuchinoko has advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks it makes in any terrain with ample obscuring plant life.

features.name: Standing Leap
features.description: The tsuchinoko's long jump is up to 15 feet and its high jump is up to 5 feet, with or without a running start.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The tsuchinoko makes two leaping bite attacks. The second attack has disadvantage and must be made against the same target as the first.

actions.name: Leaping Bite
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 1 piercing damage plus 5 (2d4) poison damage.

actions.name: Hoop Form
actions.description: The tsuchinoko bites its tail, forming a hoop with its body. While in hoop form, the tsuchinoko has a walking speed of 60 feet and can't make leaping bite attacks. The tsuchinoko can end its hoop form as a bonus action.

monsters.name: Vallowex
monsters.senses: blindsight 60 ft. (blind beyond this radius), passive Perception 14

features.name: Amphibious
features.description: The vallowex can breathe air and water.

features.name: Aura of Thirst
features.description: At the start of each of the vallowex's turns, each creature within 30 feet of it must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or have disadvantage on its next attack roll or ability check as a gnawing thirst distracts it. For each minute a creature stays in the vallowex's aura, it gains one level of exhaustion from dehydration. A level of exhaustion is removed if the creature uses an action to drink 1 pint of water. A vallowex is immune to its own Aura of Thirst as well as the auras of other vallowexes.

features.name: Underwater Camouflage
features.description: The vallowex has advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks made while underwater.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The vallowex makes two attacks: one with its spiked tongue and one with its tail.

actions.name: Spiked Tongue
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. Hit: 14 (2d8 + 5) piercing damage, and the target is grappled (escape DC 15). Until this grapple ends, the target is restrained, and the vallowex can't use its spiked tongue against another target.

actions.name: Tail
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 16 (2d10 + 5) bludgeoning damage.

actions.name: Swallow
actions.description: The vallowex makes one spiked tongue attack against a Medium or smaller target it is grappling. If the attack hits, the target is also swallowed, and the grapple ends. The swallowed target is blinded and restrained, it has total cover against attacks and other effects outside the vallowex, and it takes 10 (3d6) acid damage at the start of each of the vallowex's turns. The vallowex can have only one creature swallowed at a time.

monsters.name: Wraith Bear
damage_resistances: bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks not made with silvered weapons
languages: the languages it knew in life

features.name: Detect Ancestors
features.description: The wraith bear knows the direction to its nearest living ancestor on the same plane, but not the ancestor's exact location.

features.name: Draining Regeneration
features.description: The wraith bear regains 10 hp at the start of its turn if it has at least 1 hp and there are living plants within 5 feet of it. When the wraith bear regains hp, all plant life within 5 feet of it dies, and it can't regain hp from those same plants again.

features.name: Incorporeal Movement
features.description: The wraith bear can move through other creatures and objects as if they were difficult terrain. It takes 5 (1d10) force damage if it ends its turn inside an object.

features.name: Undead Nature
features.description: A wraith bear doesn't require air, food, drink, or sleep.

actions.name: Life Drain
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 31 (6d8 + 4) necrotic damage. The target must succeed on a DC 16 Constitution saving throw or its hp maximum is reduced by an amount equal to the damage taken. This reduction lasts until the target finishes a long rest. The target dies if this effect reduces its hp maximum to 0.

actions.name: Baleful Roar (Recharge 6)
actions.description: The bear lets out a supernatural roar in a 30-foot cone. Each creature in that area that can hear the bear must make a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, a creature is incapacitated for 1 minute. On a success, a creature is frightened until the end of its next turn. An incapacitated creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

npcs.name: Anya Gristlegrot

features.name: Cursing Stick
features.description: Cursing Stick (recharges after a long rest). Anya points a gnarled wooden stick at a single creature within 30 feet and utters a powerful curse. If the creature fails a DC 12 Wisdom saving throw, Anya polymorphs the target into a giant frog, or transforms its head into a donkey's. The target remains under the curse until it fulfills a special challenge set by Anya (e.g. stealing a leprechaun's pot of gold, winning a race with a quickling), the target drops to 0 hp or dies, or Anya's cursing stick is destroyed. The cursing stick is AC 15 and has 10 hp. It takes Anya a day to craft a replacement. The cursed creature is limited in the actions it can perform by the nature of its new form, and cannot speak.

npcs.description: This nine-foot-tall ogress has greenish skin, a bulbous nose covered in pimples, and a mouth filled with crooked and broken teeth. She reeks of a heady combination of sweat and patchouli. Anya has few friends among the other revelers. She resents most fey, particularly elves, for looking down their perfectly formed noses at her, and likes nothing more than to see them taken down a peg or two. Anya hates the Holly Queen for humiliating her at the last winter revels and longs for revenge. She spends a lot of time brooding on her lowly status, and is quick to anger, but can be won over with flattery focusing on how fearsome and devious she is. Anya sometimes has potions and other minor magic items for sale. Anya has the stats of a green hag, but her size is Large.
npcs.source: Wrath of the River King p.37

npcs.name: Gerribbit

features.name: Curse of the Cursing Stick
features.description: Gerribbit is cursed to remain a frog until he wins a big, slobbery kiss from a hairy dwarf, half-orc, or satyr. He has had no luck so far but that doesn't stop him from leaping beside any suitable character in the hopes they will kiss him. Gerribbit tries his best to communicate with the characters but can only say "gerribbit." If they are able to talk to him with speak with animals, he explains his predicament and begs for their help. If Gerribbit returns to his true form, he will tell them that events in the nearby human village of Riverbend have angered the River King, and its inhabitants may soon come under attack by the fey; see Wrath of the River King.

npcs.description: Until a few days ago, Gerribbit was Solanquis, a young and arrogant minor elf noble at the River King's Court. Now he is a giant frog. The foppish youth made the mistake of upsetting Anya Gristlegrot by failing to treat her with respect, and the angry ogress polymorphed the hapless elf into his present form with her cursing stick.
npcs.source: Wrath of the River King p.37

npcs.name: Holly Queen

features.name: Holly Queen's Badge
features.description: The winners of the dancing contest at the winter revel each get to dance with the Holly Queen in turn. As they twirl around together, she will whisper in their ear, asking them if they are willing to wear her badge. Those that say yes may find themselves performing a service for the queen in the future and may even be whisked off to spend the summer months at her castle in the Shadow Realm.

features.name: Pumpkin Jack's Candle
features.description: The Holly Queen has been given Pumpkin Jack's candle by a pombero (see Tome of Beasts) named Gloamwalker who wanted to curry favor with her. If the characters ask her respectfully, she is willing to exchange it for a "small service." The Holly Queen has heard whispers of goblin raids and kidnappings in the human village of Riverbend and would like the characters to find out what is going on; see Wrath of the River King.

npcs.description: This raven-haired shadow fey enchantress (see Tome of Beasts) is a guest of honor at the winter revel, and usually attends the spring and autumn revels, but is seen at the summer revel only rarely. She wears a holly crown with bright red berries on her horned head, and dresses in long black robes adorned with winter wolf fur. A tiny robin redbreast perches on her shoulder. The Holly Queen is a loyal vassal of the Moonlit King, and is out of favor at the Courts of the Shadow Fey while the Queen of Night and Magic and her Summer Court are in the ascendant. Quiet, observant, and somewhat sorrowful, she comes to the revels to keep abreast of affairs among the elves of the Arbonesse and to gather intelligence on the River Court.
npcs.source: Wrath of the River King p.37

npcs.name: Pumpkin Jack
npcs.description: This fey bogeyman makes his home in the Shadow Realm, venturing into the Material Plane to frighten mortals at the behest of his mistress, the Queen of Night and Magic. A terrifying figure with a grinning, evil-looking jack-o-lantern for a head and long, wicked
npcs.source: Wrath of the River King p.37

npcs.name: Terelsa Garlook

features.name: Go-Between
features.description: Terelsa Garlook is a go-between, an agent who knows how to hire the right people for any sort of job: domestic, dangerous, mundane, or odd. Although she avoids strictly illegal commissions, she sometimes works for less than savory characters who often want, for obvious reasons, to remain anonymous. She also does occasional work for the city government.

npcs.description: Terelsa Garlook is a go-between, an agent who knows how to hire the right people for any sort of job: domestic, dangerous, mundane, or odd. Although she avoids strictly illegal commissions, she sometimes works for less than savory characters who often want, for obvious reasons, to remain anonymous. She also does occasional work for the city government.

npcs.name: Baba Migori

features.name: Wild Shape (Air Elemental)
features.description: She actually turns into an air elemental and flies away through the trees.

npcs.description: Baba Migori, also called Grandmother Migori, is a powerful druid who is very familiar with the forest. She often tests travelers for their worthiness. Uninterested in fighting, she quickly disappears in the wind if attacked.

npcs.name: Elsee Barkcot

features.name: Irrational Fear of Spiders
features.description: She has an irrational fear of spiders.

npcs.description: Elsee Barkcot is the mother of a bearfolk family living in a small cottage just north of a clearing. Her youngest son, Obiah, is trapped in a tree by a giant spider.

npcs.name: Frauleene

features.name: Injured Leg
features.description: She is not armed and has an injured leg. She can only just keep ahead of the savage ogre that wants to torment and consume her.

npcs.description: Frauleene is a young, female alseid and an herbalist. She was caught off guard by an ogre while gathering plants in the forest. She knows where to find Queen's Glade and can lead the characters in that direction.

npcs.name: Mother Babushka

features.name: Fortune Telling
features.description: If anyone asks to have their fortune told, she has that individual drip candle wax into a bowl of cold water, then examines the shapes that form: "I see choice, catechism, and consequences. You will pass through places that were old before iron was born, and iron will avail you little there. Knowledge of the Old Ways is better than sword or shield. I'll also say this: Not all that's devoured is dead and gone, and when offered a choice, the brave may earn a great reward by boldly saying 'All'."

features.name: Knowledge of the Challenge of the Fang
features.description: She knows that the Challenge of the Fang involves a battle with the Would-Be-King of Wolves and tests in a sacred place called the Paths of Gamayun.

npcs.description: Mother Babushka is a woman so tiny and wrinkled that she looks like a gnome, almost buried beneath a cloak of owl feathers and layers of patterned cloth. Patches of moss and wood-like nubs mark her olive skin, a sure sign of someone who has drunk deep of the Margreve's power.

npcs.name: Hodel Köhler

features.name: Poor at Concealing Truth
features.description: He has a –1 penalty on Charisma (Deception) checks.

equipment: small tin box that's warm to the touch
npcs.description: The tearful man is Hodel Köhler, drowning his sorrows in cheap liquor. Nervously wringing his hands, he soon approaches the party, then bursts into tears, begging for help. He says that his daughter has become lost in the forest, and no one dares go look for her.

npcs.name: Boleslav

features.name: Šestaci
features.description: A wicked man with six fingers on each hand who can see the true form of ala and serves their evil whims.

features.name: Werewolf
features.description: Boleslav is a werewolf.

equipment: amulet of lightning-struck stone in the shape of an ala (50 gp)
npcs.description: Their leader, Boleslav, is a werewolf and also a šestaci—a wicked man with six fingers on each hand who can see the true form of ala and serves their evil whims.

npcs.name: Tanya

features.name: Subtle Spell
features.description: Tanya can choose to cast a spell without the required verbal and/or somatic components.

features.name: Quickened Spell
features.description: When casting a spell that has a casting time of 1 action, Tanya can change the casting time to 1 bonus action for this casting.

features.name: Spellcasting
features.description: Tanya is a 6th-level spellcaster. Her spellcasting ability is Charisma (spell save DC 15, +7 to hit with spell attacks). She has the following spells prepared: Cantrips (at will): dancing lights, douse light (see Heroes Handbook), fire bolt, mending, prestidigitation; 1st level (4 slots): comprehend languages, identify, mage armor; 2nd level (3 slots): alter self, detect thoughts; 3rd level (3 slots): clairvoyance, fear

actions.name: Quarterstaff
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +2 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 2 (1d6 – 1) bludgeoning damage, or 3 (1d8 – 1) bludgeoning damage if wielded with two hands.

npcs.description: Tanya is a chaotic neutral human spellcaster.

npcs.name: Jędza

features.name: Fascinate
features.description: When the vila sings, all those within 60 feet of her and who can hear her must make a successful DC 14 Charisma saving throw or be stunned for 1d4 rounds. Those who succeed on the saving throw are immune to that vila's singing for 24 hours.

features.name: Forest Song
features.description: The vila magically calls 2d6 wolves or 2 wampus cats (see Tome of Beasts). The called creatures arrive in 1d4 rounds, acting as allies of the vila and obeying its spoken commands. The beasts remain for 1 hour, until the vila dies, or until the vila dismisses them as a bonus action.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: Jędza makes two quarterstaff attacks or two shortbow attacks.

actions.name: +1 Quarterstaff
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) bludgeoning damage, or 6 (1d8 + 2) bludgeoning damage if wielded with two hands.

actions.name: +1 Shortbow
actions.description: Ranged Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, range 80/320 ft., one target. Hit: 9 (1d6 + 6) piercing damage.

spellcasting.description: 1st level: friendship, entangle, fog cloud, longstrider. 2nd level (3 slots): calm emotions, animal messenger, hold person

npcs.description: A vila (Jędza) with spellcasting and singing abilities.

traps.name: A Floor of Honey
traps.trigger: The wax floor of the tunnel is rigged to break when stepped on, trapping the feet of trespassers in a glue-like honey.

detection.detail: Spotting the trap requires a successful DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check.

disarm.detail: The trap cannot be disabled, but it can be avoided.

traps.effect: If the trap is triggered, the character must make a successful DC 12 Dexterity saving throw to avoid falling through and becoming grappled (escape DC 12).
traps.area: The wax floor of the tunnel, just 10 feet beyond the meeting room.
traps.description: A wax floor rigged to break when stepped on, trapping the feet of trespassers in a glue-like honey.

traps.name: A Thin Floor and a Short Fall
traps.trigger: The wax floor is constructed in such a way as to break when someone reaches the designated area.

detection.detail: Spotting the trap requires a DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check.

disarm.detail: The trap cannot be disabled, but it can be avoided.

traps.effect: Old giant bee stingers line the floor at the bottom of the pit, embedded in wax. Avoiding the stingers requires a successful DC 12 Dexterity saving throw. A character who is unable to avoid the stingers takes 3 (1d6) piercing damage and must make a DC 10 Constitution saving throw, taking 7 (2d6) poison damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
traps.description: A wax floor constructed to break when someone reaches the designated area, dropping them onto old giant bee stingers embedded in wax at the bottom of a pit.

traps.name: Thin Wax Floor
traps.trigger: The wax floor is constructed to break when someone reaches the designated area.

detection.detail: Spotting the trap and avoiding it requires a DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check.

traps.effect: Those who are caught in it fall 20 feet, taking 2d6 bludgeoning damage. The soft earthen walls of the pit make getting out difficult, requiring a DC 25 Strength (Athletics) check. If the characters attempt to climb out at the corners, the DC is decreased to 20.
traps.description: This hallway has been trapped to prevent intruders from reaching the chambers of the Honey Queen.

traps.name: Rusted Ladder (D1 Scrying Room)
traps.trigger: The first creature to climb the ladder to E2 causes it to break.

detection.detail: It takes a successful DC 25 Wisdom (Perception) check to determine that the ladder to E2 is rusted through.

traps.effect: The ladder breaks and the creature falls, taking 1d6 bludgeoning damage from the fall unless it succeeds on a DC 17 Dexterity saving throw.
traps.area: The ladder between D1 and E2.
traps.description: A rusted-through ladder that breaks when first climbed, causing a fall.

traps.name: Enchanted Mandrake Root
traps.trigger: A non-plant creature comes within 20 feet of the mandrake root.

detection.detail: Once characters have encountered their first mandrake root, they can pick their way safely through the others with successful DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) checks.

disarm.method: Impaling it with an iron pin
disarm.detail: It can be disarmed by impaling it with an iron pin.

traps.effect: A root screams (as an alarm spell) when a non-plant creature comes within 20 feet. If a mandrake root is destroyed or uprooted, it becomes the point of origin of a DC12 thunderclap spell (see Heroes Handbook).
traps.description: The King of Thorns' first line of defense is a scattering of enchanted mandrake roots: Tiny humanoid-like plants that shriek if anyone passes near. The mandrake roots are living plants with AC 5 and 4 hit points apiece.

traps.name: Door of Thorns
traps.trigger: Breaking the door open or dealing more than 10 damage to it.

detection.detail: The door is enchanted to respond to commands from the King of Thorns or his briar men.

disarm.detail: Entry can be gained by destroying it (AC 11, 30 hit points), breaking it open (requiring a successful DC 19 Strength check), or unweaving the vines (requiring a successful DC 21 Dexterity [Sleight of Hand] check).

traps.effect: Thorns emerge and attack the nearest creature. The thorns are +8 to hit, deal 3d6 piercing damage on a hit, and a target hit is also grappled (escape DC 15).
traps.description: A mass of taut vines held together by a tangle of interlocked spines forms a thorny mesh door. Breaking the door open or dealing more than 10 damage to it causes thorns to emerge and attack the nearest creature.

traps.name: Flailing Thorns
traps.trigger: Entering the warded area (areas BP1, TP4, TP5)
traps.effect: Flailing thorns attack creatures in the area
traps.area: Wards areas BP1, TP4, and TP5
traps.description: A magical trap that wards several chambers in the Briar Palace with flailing thorns.

traps.name: Deadfall Trap
traps.trigger: A creature steps into the trapped area.

detection.detail: DC 15 Wisdom (Survival) to create; presumably similar to detect.

disarm.detail: DC 15 Wisdom (Survival) to create; disarm method not specified.

traps.effect: Target must make a DC 12 Dexterity save to avoid; damage varies according to depth of the pit and what is at the bottom of it.
traps.description: A deadfall trap created from fallen logs and dead saplings.

traps.name: Unstable Log Trap
traps.trigger: A creature enters the trapped area.

detection.detail: DC 15 Wisdom (Survival) to create; presumably similar to detect.

disarm.detail: DC 15 Wisdom (Survival) to create; disarm method not specified.

traps.effect: Target must make a DC 12 Dexterity save or be knocked prone.
traps.description: An unstable log trap created from fallen logs and dead saplings.
